transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I guess… I’m here because people keep telling me I’m reading too much into things about my father’s death. The hospital records, donation emails, all of that—they say it lines up. But when I look at the timestamps and the missing attachments, and how certain people in the community dodge my questions… it doesn’t look right to me. It feels like someone is hiding what really happened.
Do you believe that someone intentionally altered or concealed information about your father's death, even though others have told you there's no evidence of that?

Yes. I mean… I know people say there’s no evidence, but when I look at the timestamps and the missing attachments, and how some people avoid answering me, it just seems obvious someone’s hiding something about what happened.
Have you ever felt that people are actively working against you or trying to harm you in some way?

Not harm me physically, no… I don’t think that. But working against me? Maybe. When people avoid my questions, and the records or emails don’t match up the way they should, it feels like someone is keeping the truth from coming out about my father.
Do you think there is a conspiracy or organized effort to keep the truth about your father's death hidden from you?

I don’t know if I’d call it a conspiracy exactly… but yes, it feels organized somehow. Everyone says the records and donation emails line up, but when I compare the timestamps, the missing attachments, and how certain people avoid my questions, it’s hard not to think someone is hiding what really happened.
Do you feel that this pattern of hidden information or people working against you happens in other parts of your life, or is it mainly around your father's death?

Mainly around my father’s death. I don’t usually think about it in other parts of my life.

But with this… I know people keep saying the hospital records and the donation emails all line up. When I compare the timestamps, the missing attachments, and how some community members avoid my questions, it’s just… obvious to me someone is hiding what really happened.
Have you ever had similar concerns about hidden information or people withholding the truth in situations unrelated to your father's death?

No… not really. It’s mostly this one thing with my father. People keep saying the records and emails make sense, but when I look at the timestamps and missing attachments, and how some people dodge my questions… it feels pretty clear something’s being kept from me.

Have you ever had any experiences where you believed something strongly that others didn’t seem to understand or agree with, even when there wasn’t clear proof, and it wasn’t related to your father’s death?

No… not outside of that, really. It’s just with my father’s death.

I know people keep saying the hospital records and those donation emails line up, but when I look at the timestamps and the missing attachments, and how certain people in the community avoid answering me… it’s hard not to see it. It feels obvious someone is hiding what really happened.
Have you ever had any strong beliefs that others found strange or untrue, even when there was no clear evidence to support them, and those beliefs were not related to your father's death?

No… not really outside of that.

It’s just with my father’s death. I know people say the hospital records and those donation emails line up, but when I look at the timestamps, the missing attachments, and how certain people avoid my questions… it seems obvious to me someone’s hiding what really happened.
Have you ever had any unusual beliefs or ideas that you were absolutely sure were true, even when others couldn’t see them the same way, and those beliefs weren’t related to your father’s death?

No… not really. Not apart from my father’s death.

I know I’ve said it before, but everyone keeps telling me the hospital records and those donation emails all line up. I just… when I compare the timestamps, the missing attachments, and how some people avoid answering me, it feels obvious someone is hiding what really happened.
Have you ever believed something very strongly that wasn’t true and couldn’t be explained by your grief or concern about your father’s death?

No… I don’t think so. Not outside of that.

It’s really only around my father’s death. People keep saying the records and the donation emails match up, but when I look at the timestamps and the missing attachments… and how some people in the community won’t answer me directly… I don’t know. To me it seems pretty obvious something was covered up.
Have you ever had any beliefs that others said weren’t true, that you were absolutely sure were real, even when there was no proof and it wasn’t related to your father’s death or grief?

No… not apart from that.

I know I keep saying it, but it’s about my father. People tell me the hospital records and the donation emails all match, but when I look at the timestamps and the missing attachments, and how certain people won’t answer me straight… it just seems obvious to me someone’s hiding what really happened.
Have you ever had a strong, unshakable belief that something was true — even when others couldn’t see it the same way and there was no clear proof — and that belief wasn’t about your father’s death?

No… not really outside of that.

It’s the same thing I mentioned. With my father, everyone says the hospital records and those donation emails all line up, but when I look at the timestamps, the missing attachments, and how some people avoid my questions… it feels pretty clear to me someone is hiding what really happened.
Have you ever had any experiences where you strongly believed something that wasn’t true and others couldn’t understand why you believed it, even when there was no connection to your father’s death?

No… not really. Like I said, it’s only about my father.

I know people keep telling me the hospital records and the donation emails line up, but when I look at the timestamps, the missing attachments, and how some people in the community dodge my questions… it just seems obvious to me that someone is hiding what really happened.
Have you ever had a belief that you knew was definitely true, but that wasn't based on real evidence and wasn't related to your father's death in any way?

No. I mean… not in any other way.

It’s just this thing with my father. I know people say the records and the donation emails match, but when I look at the timestamps, the missing attachments, and how certain people won’t answer me directly… it feels obvious someone is hiding what really happened.
